text:
sophia: hit a weird failure today in canary where spans from tenant B never arrived in OTLP collector after we triggered a manual kv-cache prefix flush. non-deterministic but reproducible locally.
sophia: stack snippet: ```
RuntimeError: cannot schedule new future after shutdown
  File "/app/worker.py", line 278, in handle
    await self.kv.flush_prefix(prefix)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/opentelemetry/exporter/otlp/async_exporter.py", line 102, in export
    await self._exporter_client.send(span_proto)
RuntimeError: cannot schedule new future after shutdown
```
ajay: are we calling tracer_provider.shutdown() while background tasks still run? python async-exporter uses loop.create_task internally which is fragile at process exit.
leah: we also saw a spike in otel.queue.drops for tenant B in metrics right around the same time. sounds like queue backpressure + aggressive shutdown.
kevin: pattern in Go worker is to transition to DRAINING state, stop accepting new requests, wait for in-flight handlers, then call exporter.Shutdown(ctx). that avoids the create_task race.
kevin: sample Go drain flow: ```go
worker.SetState(DRAINING)
listener.Close() // stop new connections
wg.Wait() // handlers finish
exporter.Shutdown(ctx)
```
yin: two angles: (1) make background flushes cooperative with exporter shutdown (register them), (2) enforce bounded queues with clear metrics and per-tenant backoff so one noisy tenant doesn't fill memory.
ajay: proposal: add a small cross-lang shim "redwood_trace_lifecycle" with APIs: `init()`, `register_drain_group(name)`, `enter_group()`, `leave_group()`, `drain_and_stop(timeout)`. kv-cache flush tasks call enter/leave so shutdown waits.
sophia: for Python implement enter/leave as an async refcount + Event that shutdown waits on. if shutdown begins, new enter() should either fail fast or block based on mode. default: fail fast and emit metric.
leah: also we need per-tenant bounded fanout queues for exporter fanout. if queue is full, increment `otel.exporter.queue_full` and drop with reason tag=tenant. console should surface tenant spikes.
kevin: Rust/Go keep blocking shutdown semantics but also register the same drain_group so the lifecycle UX is consistent. this avoids surprises when teams move between runtimes.
yin: retention/ingest note: if exporter drops spans, downstream retention calc will lose signals (alerts, SLOs). add a pipeline metric `otel.ingest.loss_reason` with tags (queue_full, shutdown, exporter_err).
ajay: rollout UX: config knobs `REDWOOD_OTEL_MODE=compat|native` and `REDWOOD_OTEL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS` so hosted defaults to compat with 5s drain to be safe. opt-in native for internal perf testing.
sophia: I'll draft a python wrapper: ```python
class DrainGroup:
    def __init__(self):
        self._count = 0
        self._draining = False
        self._event = asyncio.Event()
    async def enter(self):
        if self._draining:
            raise RuntimeError('shutdown')
        self._count += 1
    async def leave(self):
        self._count -= 1
        if self._count == 0 and self._draining:
            self._event.set()
    async def drain_wait(self, timeout):
        self._draining = True
        if self._count == 0:
            return
        await asyncio.wait_for(self._event.wait(), timeout)
```
This prevents create_task races by failing new background flushes once drain starts.
leah: add GH action lint to fail on any new exporter that uses unbounded queue buffer in our runner images. small perf tradeoff but safety first.
yin: alerting rule for console: fire when `rate(otel.exporter.queue_full[1m]) > 5` for any tenant OR `otel.ingest.loss_reason{reason="shutdown"} > 0` in last 5m.
ajay: tests: (1) flaky reproduction test that spawns N concurrent kv flush + span exporters then triggers drain. master should throw, shim should pass. (2) e2e canary with `REDWOOD_OTEL_MODE=compat` for 24h.
otel-bot: created deploy-ticket OTEL-LIFECYCLE-SHIM, canary env=eng-runtime, owner=@ajay
sophia: I'll open the python PR tomorrow with the drain wrapper + unit tests and CI lint. tagging infra for GH action change.
kevin: agree. once canary stable we'll flip hosted default to compat then communicate in #all-hands so platform teams can plan. :thumbsup:
